hints: A ) is unpaired when no ( is waiting before it. Which ( are unpaired? The ones still waiting when the scan ends.
Use a stack of indices of open brackets. Mark unpaired ) positions during the scan and leftover ( positions at the end, then rebuild the string without them.

1. Create a stack of indices and a boolean[] drop.
  2. For (: push its index.
  3. For ): if the stack is empty mark it in drop, else pop.
  4. After the scan, mark every index left on the stack.
  5. Build the answer from the characters not marked.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try removing subsets of brackets, smallest subsets first, until the string is balanced.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One scan with a stack of open-bracket indices pairs brackets exactly as the statement describes; unpaired ones are skipped when rebuilding.

explain: For s = "x)(y(z)": the ) at index 1 finds an empty stack, so it is dropped. The ( at 2 and at 4 are pushed. The ) at 6 pops index 4, pairing them. Index 2 is left on the stack, so it is dropped too. Keeping the rest gives "xy(z)". Each ) takes the nearest unpaired (, which is exactly what popping the top of the stack does. For "))a((" every bracket is dropped, leaving just "a".
recognize: Matching parentheses and deleting the ones without a partner → stack of open-bracket positions.
